title: Tidebone Crossing
description: Three closed limestone vaults, each formed by two tapered limbs meeting at the crown, stand on fractured stone footings.

review.notes: Lead extra round (final). Fixed: the smooth polished tubes are gone; the ribs are now rough, eroded limestone with weathering (grime and lichen at the feet, streaks, darker recesses), and each foot flares into a fused buttress root instead of loose shards (t9, closeup). The figure now stands at the rib foot in the base view, so scale reads. Still failing: (1) defects 7: each rib stands in a smooth olive turf cone with a lobed star outline and a clean hard edge on the ground, sprinkled with black specks for grass (t9, hero), the same placeholder-base problem rejected on the vegetation; (2) form_detail/style 7: one even crumpled-noise relief of the same frequency covers every rib from foot to crown, like papier-mache, with no bedding lines, larger fracture planes or smoother wind-worn crowns. Fix: replace the cones with a low, irregular soil-and-turf patch that fades into the ground, with real grass tufts, scree and chalk chips; add 2-3 scales of relief (horizontal bedding bands and a few large fracture faces on the lower third, smoother worn surfaces toward the crown).
